summary.headline: Dr. Lal PathLabs Q2 FY27 revenue rose 19.6% to Rs 874 crore, its fastest quarterly growth in five years, with EBITDA margin at 32.1%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue reached Rs 874 crore (up 19.6% YoY) on 9% patient volume growth, with revenue per patient up 9.7% to Rs 976. EBITDA rose 25.1% to Rs 280 crore (32.1% margin) and PAT rose 27.5% to Rs 194 crore. Management said H1 is running ahead of plan and now expects FY27 revenue growth in the high teens and EBITDA margin slightly above FY26's 27.2%. The company completed the SN GeneLab acquisition (70% stake), bought out the remaining 30% of Centrapath Labs, acquired Sunshine Diagnostics in Ghana and formed a JV in Uzbekistan.

segments.name: Patient volumes and samples
segments.commentary: Sample volume rose 13.6% to 28.8 million and patient volume rose 9% to 9 million in Q2 FY27. Management said patient growth was above 8% in both Q1 and Q2 and came across the country.

segments.name: Tier 3 and below
segments.commentary: Management said about 39-40% of revenue comes from Tier 3 towns and below, and that the company is gaining share there.

segments.name: Suburban and West
segments.commentary: Suburban is back to double-digit growth, and West growth is better than before. Management said the company is investing in Suburban infrastructure.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: International business is under 5% of revenue, with management expecting it to remain around that level in 2-3 years. It includes the Sunshine Diagnostics acquisition in Ghana and a JV in Uzbekistan.

segments.name: Sovaaka and radiology
segments.commentary: Sovaaka is a single-centre operation still under development and is not reported separately. Radiology (CT/MRI) is run as a patient-retention service across two pilot centres, not a standalone investment.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth now expected in the high teens (previously guided mid-teens organic over the medium term); H1 is running slightly ahead of plan.
FY27 EBITDA margin expected to be slightly better than FY26's 27.2%; earlier guidance was 27-28%, which management did not explicitly update.
Long-term organic revenue growth framed as mid-teens: 6-7% patient volume plus 6-7% price/geography/mix benefit.
CGHS price-increase benefit of 2-3% to revenue growth is expected to continue for about one more quarter, then become part of organic growth.

Gross margin trajectory of the past four quarters is not expected to continue given inflationary costs (dollar, geopolitics). FY28 guidance not yet finalised; management will give directional view in 1-2 quarters.
Interim dividend of Rs 5 per share (50%) declared, the second interim dividend.
capex_capacity: Opened 32 labs over the last two years; plans to open about 15-18 more labs in FY27.
SN GeneLab (Surat) acquired in August 2026, with 70% stake; FY26 revenue about Rs 60 crore and EBITDA about Rs 15 crore; remaining 30% via put and call option, timing not disclosed.
Centrapath Labs: remaining 30% stake acquired, now wholly owned.
Rural outreach programme active in seven states with higher patient numbers this quarter.
Digital pathology foundation established on a hybrid cloud platform integrated with LIMS, with a new physical report format reaching more than 80% of patients daily.
Launched around 140 new tests in H1 FY27, including two first-in-India assays in Q2.
demand_pricing: Management said industry demand has some buoyancy, and the reach from lab and collection-centre expansion is a contributing factor.

No price increase taken for more than 4 years; management said a future increase would be below inflation on a CAGR basis, with triggers being cost pressure and market price-benchmark movement, not timing.
Competition described as persistently high, mainly from unorganised players rather than metro organised peers.
Specialised tests are priced higher, but management does not expect their share of the mix to keep rising.

qa_highlights.question: Rationale for the SN GeneLab valuation, which an analyst estimated at about 5x trailing EBITDA-to-sales.
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it a strategic fit in genomics and said the EBITDA multiple is better than comparable peer deals. It is a profitable business. Further valuation questions were taken offline.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 9% patient growth driven by Tier 3, specialised menus or the unorganised-to-organised shift?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth is across the country and reflects market buoyancy plus network and collection-centre expansion over 2-3 years. Specialised tests help differentiation but are not expected to rise as a share of mix.

qa_highlights.question: How much does the CGHS price hike contribute?
qa_highlights.answer: It adds 2-3% to revenue growth in Q2 and is expected to last about one more quarter before becoming organic growth.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company take a price hike, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: No fixed timing such as Q4. Triggers are cost pressure (dollar, PF/gratuity regulatory changes) or a shift in market price benchmarks; management will re-evaluate in 1-2 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin beat an opportunity to pull back investments?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins are ahead of expectations. Management may fast-track and invest more in the business in H2 to sustain revenue growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the international contribution and outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: International is under 5% of revenue and is expected to stay near that level for 2-3 years. Ghana and Uzbekistan are longer-term plays, and overseas acquisitions are on the table.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from inflation (USD, geopolitics), wage and PF rule changes, and transport and logistics costs; other expenses rose from about Rs 120-125 crore a quarter to Rs 164 crore in Q2.
Growth may normalise from Q3-Q4 as the CGHS benefit (2-3%) laps.
Valuation and returns on SN GeneLab (premium multiple questioned) and the timing and price of the remaining 30% put/call.
South India remains about 6% of revenue, with no inorganic deal yet; organic efforts continue.
Deployment of the Rs 1,746 crore net cash pile, with management hinting at larger M&A deals.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volumes and H1 execution, with guidance raised to high-teens revenue growth. Cautious on gross margin and price increases, and evasive on valuation (referred offline), FY28 planning and the Sovaaka revenue split.
key_quotes: This is the highest quarterly growth in the last 5 years and has been driven by a 9% growth in patient volumes.
We continue to retain a significant pricing headroom as a strategic lever going forward.

So, the short answer is yes. We will continue on these initiatives, but we are looking at them more as a long-term revenue contributor, not really in the short term, not in the next 2, 3 years' time horizon.
There is no philosophical issue in terms of taking a price increase.

growth.why: Management now guides FY27 revenue growth to high teens (midpoint ~17%) with H1 revenue up 19.4% and running slightly ahead of plan, backed by patient volume growth above 8% in both quarters, 15-18 planned lab additions, and a 2-3% CGHS price benefit lasting about one more quarter; specific capacity and timing are given but no order book or utilisation figures were disclosed.

rows.label: Margin expansion

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Management plans to open about 15-18 labs in FY27 after 32 over the last two years, and the SN GeneLab (Surat) acquisition adds ~Rs 60 crore FY26 revenue; no capacity utilisation figure was disclosed to size the need.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Patient volumes grew above 8% in both Q1 and Q2 and were up 9% to 9 million in Q2, with management guiding a 6-7% long-term patient volume growth rate that it has held.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue growth guidance was already raised to high teens (about 17% midpoint) with H1 at +19.4% and running slightly ahead of plan, so further upward revision depends on sustaining the Q2 pace.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Growth may normalise from Q3-Q4 as the 2-3% CGHS price benefit laps after about one more quarter, and gross margin pressure from inflation is expected to end the recent improvement trend.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Around 140 new tests were launched in H1 FY27, including two first-in-India assays in Q2, and management is expected to keep adding specialised menus, though it does not expect their share of mix to keep rising.

rows.label: Price increase timing undecided
rows.why: No price hike in more than 4 years, with management to re-evaluate in 1-2 quarters; triggers are cost pressure (USD, PF/gratuity) or market benchmark moves, and any increase would be below inflation on a CAGR basis.

rows.label: Further M&A using Rs 1,746 crore net cash
rows.why: Management hinted at larger M&A deals, and the 30% SN GeneLab put/call and South India (about 6% of revenue, no inorganic deal yet) are open; timing and price of the put/call were not disclosed.
